value.name: Lucia reads memorandum slowly
value.description: Lucia reads the memorandum carefully and laboriously, pausing over technical terms as she works through the text.
evidence: Lucia read slowly, going back over phrases, her lips moving very faintly on the technical terms.

value.name: Rosa reads memorandum cautiously
value.description: Rosa reads the memorandum at a deliberate pace, showing unfamiliarity with formal English but no embarrassment about it.
evidence: Rosa read at the pace of a woman who had not been asked, often, to read formal English, and who was not embarrassed by her pace but who was conserving herself, taking the words one at a time, deciding about each one.

value.name: Daniel finishes reading first
value.description: Daniel completes the memorandum before the others and silently sets it down, waiting for what comes next.
evidence: Daniel finished first.
He set the memorandum down.
He did not speak. He waited.

value.name: Asha notes Daniel's progress
value.description: Asha privately recognizes that Daniel has learned from the previous day and is applying that lesson now.
evidence: Asha noted, with a small flicker of professional approval she did not let show, that he had learned something yesterday and was using it today.

value.name: Lucia finishes and acknowledges Asha
value.description: Lucia finishes reading second and silently signals acknowledgment to Asha with a nod.
evidence: Lucia finished second.
She looked up at Asha and nodded once.

value.name: Rosa rereads the opening paragraph
value.description: After finishing, Rosa returns to the beginning of the memorandum and rereads the first paragraph before speaking.
evidence: Rosa took another four minutes.
When she reached the end she went back to the beginning and read the first paragraph again.

value.name: Rosa asks about right of first refusal
value.description: Rosa raises a question about whether keeping the house would require buying out the other beneficiaries' shares.
evidence: "I have a question," she said.
"The right of first refusal. If I wanted to keep the house — I am only asking. I do not say that I do. If I wanted to keep the house, I would have to pay the other two for their shares."

value.name: Asha confirms fair market valuation
value.description: Asha confirms that the buyout would be based on the appraisal's fair market value.
evidence: "Yes."
"At fair market value."
"As established by the appraisal, yes."

value.name: Rosa recognizes she cannot afford buyout
value.description: Rosa concludes that the amount required to keep the house would be beyond her means.
evidence: "Which would be a number I cannot pay."

value.name: Asha explains possible financing options
value.description: Asha carefully explains that the buyout might still be possible depending on appraisal results, financing, and whether the others accept installment payments secured by the property.
evidence: "It might be," Asha said carefully.
"It depends on the appraisal, on the financing options available to you, on whether the other beneficiaries are willing to accept a payment over time secured by the property itself.
There are configurations in which it would be possible.
There are configurations in which it would not
